title: Live updates: Bitcoin falls back to $82,000 after inflation rises more than forecast
summary: Title: Live updates: Bitcoin falls back to $82,000 after inflation rises more than forecast URL Source: https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/10/14/live-updates-bitcoin-tumbles-from-near-usd84-000-ahead-of-u-s-inflation-data Published Time: 2026-10-14T09:45:53.438Z Markdown Content: coverage ended Oct 14, 2026, 5:00 p.m. EDT An historic turnaround lower in interest rates suggests the possibility that the bond bear market may have run its course. ![Image 1: Stephen Alpher](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F9c64385838f127845d0783e09a18548c2b886ce2-512x512.png%3Fw%3D64%26h%3D64%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint%26auto%3Dformat&w=96&q=75) ## Remarkable bond market turnaround could signal next leg up for crypto The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield is trading lower by 2.6 basis points at 5.191% shortly after the close of U.S. stocks. In the wake of the hot inflation report this morning, it had risen as high as 5.36%. How rare is that sort of turnaround? [According to Bespoke](https://x.com/bespokeinvest/status/2110432954413715522), it’s the first time since December 2022 that the 10-year yield rose 10 or more basis points and then fell 10 or more basis points from that intraday high to finish lower on the day. What’s it mean? No one knows for sure, but in the old commodity pits, these sorts of “outside days” often signaled key trend reversals. If, in fact, the long run higher in interest rates has run its course, risk assets — crypto obviously included — could stand to benefit. * * * ![Image 2: Stephen Alpher](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F9c64385838f127845d0783e09a18548c2b886ce2-512x512.png%3Fw%3D64%26h%3D64%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint%26auto%3Dformat&w=96&q=75) ## Fed's Goolsbee: Inflation numbers 'discouraging,' but need more data This morning’s stronger-than-forecast CPI report was “discouraging,” said Austan Goo
